subject: general
question: The primary sector saw uneven regional development during 1947-91. Which region benefitted the most from the Green Revolution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Northern India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Green Revolution** was introduced in India during the 1960s to address the issue of food security and increase agricultural productivity.
 
• It primarily benefitted regions with better irrigation facilities and fertile soil, making **Northern India** the most successful region in adopting and reaping its benefits.
 
• States like **Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh** saw a significant boost in agricultural production, particularly in crops like wheat and rice. *Hence, Northern India benefitted the most from the Green Revolution.*
 
• **Technological advancements** such as the introduction of high-yield variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and better irrigation systems contributed to the agricultural boom in Northern India.
 
• The Green Revolution was concentrated in regions with access to irrigation, which was abundantly available in Northern India through canals and tubewells. *This made Northern India the focal point of the Green Revolution.*
 
• Although other regions like Western, Eastern, and Southern India saw some benefits, they did not experience the same level of agricultural transformation as Northern India due to a lack of adequate irrigation and infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Impact of Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution transformed **India’s agricultural sector**, making the country self-sufficient in food grains production.
 
• It led to **increased productivity**, particularly in wheat and rice, and reduced dependence on imports.
 
• Northern India became the **granary of the country**, producing surplus food grains to meet domestic and export demands.
 
 
 
• **Regional Factors:**
 
 
• Regions with better irrigation systems like **Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh** benefitted the most due to their ability to implement advanced agricultural techniques.
 
• Areas in **Eastern and Southern India** lagged behind because of inadequate irrigation, infrastructure, and less focus on Green Revolution technologies.
 
 
 
• **Technologies Introduced:**
 
 
• **High-Yield Variety (HYV) seeds:** Increased productivity and resistance to pests.
 
• **Fertilizers and pesticides:** Improved crop health and yield.
 
• **Irrigation methods:** Tubewells and canals ensured consistent water supply.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Social and Economic Impact:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution contributed to **economic growth** in Northern India, creating employment opportunities and boosting incomes for farmers.
 
• It reduced **poverty** and improved the standard of living for many rural households in Northern India.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Overdependence on irrigation led to **water depletion** in regions like Punjab and Haryana.
 
• Excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides caused **soil degradation** and environmental pollution.
